items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Then I went to work for an old Russian named Romansky. He was a photo engraver and used to work for the newspaper.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was a cigar maker. See, I was starting used to work for my uncle first -- in the cigar business, and I started from the ground up. I started to strip tobacco, sift it, sweep the building, and I started to breaking bunches. Then I started to roll them. Then I started making them for myself. And then I went out in the big factory and I was working -- I started on the cheap job which sometimes was $8 a thousand. Then the big job was $50 a thousand. You had to be almost perfect, that when you roll them you…

And then the old men, they smoking cigars all through it. They didn't want no ventilation and they spit on the floor and the tobacco's on the floor and all that. And I saw all that and I began to get disgusted and sick of -- and I just quit.
